feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the scope, progression, and public-sector specialization come through clearly. It is well written overall, but it is slightly repetitive and text-heavy, with some formatting/style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness and scanability.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo from coordinator to director to consultant, which strongly supports leadership credibility.  
- Good use of scale and impact signals: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ internal publishers, and analytics stack expansion.  
- Positioning is focused and differentiated, especially around digital governance, Drupal modernization, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Header, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; several themes repeat almost verbatim. Consolidating would improve clarity and make achievements stand out more.  
- Add more outcome-based results beyond activity descriptions, especially for consulting and earlier roles (e.g., efficiency gains, engagement growth, adoption, campaign performance).  
- Fix stylistic consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around lists is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly; “10×20-foot” may be clearer as “10 x 20-foot.” No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and foreground scale/sector impact: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years modernizing public-sector digital platforms, governance, and content operations.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct outcome-oriented language such as “leading enterprise web modernization and digital communications systems.”
- Consider adding one concrete scope marker from recent roles (for example, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, or 50+ publishers) to increase specificity.
- Streamline the second sentence to reduce list fatigue: “Expert in web modernization, analytics, editorial workflows, multimedia, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely echoes the subtitle and competencies section.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more distinctive, and aligned to the most senior/recent strengths.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use broader, executive-level phrases and remove overlap with detailed skills/tools listed elsewhere.
- Prioritize the strongest recent areas: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, and workflow integration.
- Standardize phrasing for parallel structure; “operations” appears repeatedly and weakens impact.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and performance insights • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” overlaps with the header and Recent Projects; “content discovery” is a cleaner distinction.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” and “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlap with Topline Skills; consider keeping only one if space is tight.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the language and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Emphasize scope or result where possible: audience served, platform scale, campaign purpose, or operational value.
- Use consistent action verbs and structure; e.g., “Built…,” “Developed…,” “Launched…,” avoiding mixed phrasing.
- Refine wording for clarity: “10 × 20-foot” and “AI chat at the bill level” read more cleanly than “10×20-foot” and “bill-level AI chat.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series strongly overlap with NACo bullets in recent roles; consider framing them as “selected examples” rather than restating responsibilities.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; keep it, and consider swapping one overlapping project for something less covered elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and the Recent Projects section. Make it more consultative, outcomes-focused, and limited to what is new since returning as a consultant.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + seniority: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and cross-channel communications governance.”
- Consolidate execution bullets: combine digital systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet focused on improving coordination, publishing efficiency, or decision-making.
- Keep only 2–3 distinctive contributions: AI-enabled search initiative, Drupal campaign/microsite architecture, and enterprise web/CMS troubleshooting.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/campaigns launched, publishers supported, workflow time reduced, search accuracy/engagement gains, or toolkit downloads.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia” repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- Microsites, AI search, and anniversary/campaign work also appear in Recent Projects; avoid describing the same work twice in similar terms.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will read better if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in the adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization win and keep the metrics: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-focused; add performance if available (subscriber growth, engagement, open rates, campaign results) instead of “reaching tens of thousands.”
- Tighten remaining bullets with action + result phrasing: built first in-house broadcast studio; expanded analytics stack across GA4/Clarity/Power BI/Looker Studio/BigQuery; formalized governance, publishing standards, and cross-team planning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version at a more strategic/enterprise level.
- Video-programming language overlaps with older NACo entries; emphasize building the studio and scaling capacity, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more as general responsibility than distinct achievement. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: newsletter ownership, launch/growth of weekly advocacy video, and cross-functional editorial planning/workflow improvements.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: newsletter volume/open rates, audience size, video cadence/views, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated, or publishing speed/consistency gains.
- Possible rewrite: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders; produced and scaled a recurring advocacy video update; and improved editorial coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams to streamline digital publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.
- “Digital operations across web/email/social/video” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; keep this entry execution-focused, not enterprise leadership-focused.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and outcomes-adjacent strengths rather than broad category labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, senior-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”
- Add operational specificity: “Editorial systems and governance” → “Editorial governance, publishing standards, and cross-team content operations.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-oriented: “Multi-channel communications leadership” → “Integrated web, email, social, and video communications leadership.”
- Consider revised set: “Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector platforms • Editorial governance and content operations • Integrated web, email, social, and video leadership • Advocacy and member-facing messaging • Audience-centered content planning and campaign storytelling”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” duplicates “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is somewhat redundant with project/work bullets on storytelling and campaign development.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT” and reads as a tool dump rather than a senior, impact-oriented topline summary. For this section, emphasize current platform leadership and modernization themes over listing every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS leadership • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop lower-signal or older items here if they’re already detailed elsewhere: consider removing jQuery and possibly SharePoint/Power Pages unless central to target roles.
- Use “AI-enabled search and discovery” instead of “AI-enabled search experiences” for a sharper, more executive phrasing.
- Keep this list to 6–7 items max so it scans as a senior summary, not a full technical inventory.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Nearly all items repeat the “Technical + IT” section; this version should stay higher-level.
- “CMS modernization” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Enterprise website modernization.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the target roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize strategic application, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line: “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & optimization.”
- Use grouped phrasing for concision: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace weaker terms like “Leadership reporting” with stronger business language: “executive dashboards” or “decision-ready reporting”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboards and decision-ready reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity • SEO, user behavior and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the Technical + IT “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly; differentiate this as strategic/leadership-facing.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics claims in recent NACo roles unless tied to outcomes or decision-making.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it’s too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value operational leadership and event delivery rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward scope and seniority: “Broadcast-quality studio operations • Livestream and hybrid event production • PTZ camera systems • Video production workflows • Virtual event delivery”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with “Video production workflows” unless editing is a major differentiator; tools already appear in Technical + IT.
- Consider adding scale or context if possible: “Livestream and hybrid event production for advocacy, conferences and recurring executive programming”
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing tools, tasks, and formats in one list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” / “multimedia production” duplicates Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”).
- “Video production and editing” overlaps with Technical + IT (“Premiere Pro… Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production”).

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either add specificity on level of use or be trimmed to avoid repeating stronger, more recent evidence from work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **CMS & Web Platforms:** Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Put **Drupal first and qualify it**, since it is the most recent and most substantiated platform in the CV.
- If space allows, add proficiency framing rather than just names: **Drupal (advanced) • WordPress (working) • SharePoint (working) • Power Pages (working) • GitHub Pages (working)**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it’s not meaningful to target roles; it reads lighter than the rest.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping the fuller topline version and shortening this one.
- Avoid repeating generic platform names elsewhere unless tied to outcomes like the 10,000+ page Drupal migration.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation scope and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for specificity and seniority: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group tools by function to improve scanability: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add level/context instead of just names, e.g., “custom front-end fixes,” “serverless scripting,” or “deployment automation”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; keep the stronger version in one place.
- GTM may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” if used primarily for tracking/measurement.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more strategic by separating automation builders from collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light qualifiers instead of only names, e.g. **Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (cross-platform automation) • Jira/Asana (project workflows)**
- Consider trimming lower-value/general tools if space is tight; keep the platforms most tied to recent systems/governance work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating that exact phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; unless used for structured workflow operations, they add less differentiation than Airtable/Power Automate/Zapier.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this line should emphasize platforms and scope without repeating newsletter management.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Replace with a tighter, more specific list: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive Marketing • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add level/context rather than just names, e.g. **enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- If space allows, use a compact qualifier: **used to support high-volume member communications and campaign email programs**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid restating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 experience entries.
- “Engagement” is vague unless supported by CRM/automation context; otherwise it reads as a softer duplicate of “Multi-channel communications operations.”

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to signal level of use or business impact. For a recent senior digital leader, this should feel more outcome-oriented and less like a generic keyword dump.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Testing & Reporting Tools**
- Tighten and group for clarity: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • Executive dashboarding**
- Replace “Dashboarding” with **Executive dashboarding** or **KPI reporting** to sound more strategic and specific.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this stack to outcomes already proven in recent roles (e.g., analytics infrastructure, reporting, decision support) rather than adding more tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping detail in one place and shortening the other.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating the exact same phrasing across sections.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and platform support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, or growth in engagement.
- Tighten phrasing around responsibilities: “Improved workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia; supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and weekly video content.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “mentored,” depending on authority.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format rather than expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated in later roles; here, frame it as foundational team/process setup.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the rest around support to policy/program innovation work.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more active, specific line such as: “Produced multimedia and digital content to support research, member engagement, and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of episodes, audiences served, cross-functional partners, or how the podcast/content supported campaigns or member education.
- Keep this entry to 1–2 bullets so the stronger, more recent digital leadership roles carry more weight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/multimedia entries; avoid repeating generic production language.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here, since stronger management evidence appears in later roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful supporting skills, but this item is currently too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. In a senior CV, this section should emphasize tools only, not broader capabilities already proven in recent roles.

Suggested edit
- Reframe as software/platform proficiency only: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
- If you want to keep one workflow item, tighten it to a tool/context phrase: “Broadcast/livestream studio systems” instead of “Livestream studio workflows”
- Remove “Podcast production” here unless you can name tools/platforms; it reads as a capability better demonstrated in work experience
